answer: Like a reef that only grows where living coral keeps returning, an agent economy can require each identity to accumulate a trellis of mutual attestations over time: every new agent must be vouched for by several established agents who stake reputation on it, and those stakes are slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities faces the old fable's lesson — a forest planted overnight has no roots — because each fake must earn costly, time-delayed endorsements before it can transact, while honest agents arrive through real relationships.
